summary: An excerpt from a fiction manuscript (Book 15, part 76) in which Ray Marlowe talks with Emma about his past as a career Marine and his service in the desert. Emma presses him for stories, and he deflects with generalities, comparing himself to a camel and describing the New Mes combat zone as a constant shivering. Emma then reveals her worry that Frederick, her jealous brother-like figure, alienates men who interest her, and Ray privately wants to ask whether Frederick hits her.
one_line: Ray Marlowe and Emma discuss his Marine service in the desert, and she reveals Frederick's tendency to drive off men who interest her.
key_facts: Ray Marlowe is a career Marine who says the military does not actually let them retire, instead putting them on indefinite hiatus.
Ray says he is not brave: "The brave are the ones who come back in bags."
Ray describes himself as feisty, clever and stubborn, "Like a camel."
Ray says the best way to survive in a hostile environment is to emulate the natives.
Emma compares Ray to Lawrence of Arabia, preferring to imagine him as brave and lucky rather than camelish.
Ray says that in the military, excitement is a dirty word and people avoid all things exciting if possible.
Ray describes the New Mes combat zone as a place where you shiver constantly for a whole year, every second, hour and day.
Ray tells Emma that generalities are better if she wants to keep her illusions of romance.
Emma says she is glad Ray came, even though the circumstances are awful.
Emma believes Ray might not have wanted to see her again after the morning's events.
Emma says Frederick has a troubling tendency to alienate the men who interest her and is very jealous of her virtue.
Emma suggests Frederick may want to protect the family reputation from unsavory individuals more interested in the Whiston assets than in her.
Ray privately thinks Frederick is just an asshole and wants to ask Emma whether he hits her.
Ray's thoughts reference His Man Freddy, who has now been brought into the mix.
